mentions.name: Nand2Tetris (part 1)
mentions.description: A project-oriented course from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (offered on Coursera) in which students implement an entire 16-bit computer in a hardware simulator using a simplified HDL, starting from a NAND gate and building up to an ALU, RAM, CPU, program counter, and an assembler for the computer's assembly language; part 2 covers a VM, OS, compiler, and high-level language. The commenter has two modules left in part 1.
mentions.source_excerpt: Nand2Tetris part 1. It is a project-oriented course from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (offered on Coursera) where you implement a whole 16-bit computer in a hardware simulator in a simplified HDL language, starting from a nand gate and ending with an ALU, RAM, CPU, program counter, and an assembler for the computer's assembly language. I only have two modules left before I finish part 1.
